speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history. To better understand the progression of your symptoms, how many days have these fever, rash, and respiratory issues been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the clarification. Did you notice any specific pattern to the facial rash, such as whether it spreads to your hands and feet, or if your joints are currently painful? 

Also, has anyone around you experienced similar cold-like symptoms recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease) caused by Parvovirus B19.

The combination of a prodromal viral illness (fever, rhinorrhea, headache) followed by a pruritic rash on the extremities and a facial rash that spares the perioral area is classic for this condition. Given the typical clinical presentation, no further testing is strictly necessary, but I can order a Parvovirus B19 IgM antibody test if you wish to confirm the diagnosis formally.
